title: GPU fleet replenishment scenarios and fallback lanes
summary: Working sheet with three replenishment scenarios (conservative, balanced, aggressive), regional safety buffers, SKU lead time bands, and proposed fallback lanes (cloud burst, reseller short-term leases). Includes order cadence suggestions and immediate action items for Q4 procurement planning.
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a working planning sheet for the GPU fleet replenishment plan for the next 12–18 months. Goal: ensure sufficient capacity across regions (US-W, US-E, EU, APAC) to meet target utilization curves while minimizing overcommitment and keeping unit cost competitive. This doc focuses on SKU mix, order cadence, lead time bands, and emergency/fallback lanes (short-term capacity options).

High level assumptions (reset Oct 2025):
- Monthly token/instance demand growth assumption: 7% mo/mo for inference-heavy routes, 3% for batch/embeddings.
- Target fleet utilization target for production SLOs: 65% sustained average (peaks allowed up to 85% with burst lanes).
- Preferred SKUs: H100-80GB (primary high perf), A100-80GB (secondary), L40s (cost-efficient for batching), RTX A5500 (edge/private deployment pool).
- Budget constraint: procurement commit cap of $12M (hardware) for next fiscal tranche (Jan–Jun 2026).

Regional inventory snapshot (approx current on-hand as of 2025-10-01):
- US-W: 480 GPUs (H100: 220, A100: 120, L40s: 100, RTX: 40)
- US-E: 260 GPUs (H100: 120, A100: 80, L40s: 40, RTX: 20)
- EU: 200 GPUs (H100: 80, A100: 70, L40s: 30, RTX: 20)
- APAC: 140 GPUs (H100: 40, A100: 50, L40s: 30, RTX: 20)
- Global spare pool (in transit or staging): 60 GPUs

Observed lead time bands (vendor + shipping + customs, empirical):
- H100-80GB: 16–26 weeks (varies heavily by vendor and allocation windows)
- A100-80GB: 8–14 weeks (more stock generally available)
- L40-series: 6–12 weeks (shortest lead if order early)
- RTX-class: 4–10 weeks (reseller channels possible)
Note: lead times spike during channel refresh periods (Nov–Feb) and when datacenter rack-space/backfill constrained.

Scenario planning (12-month horizon) — outputs = recommended order windows, tranche sizes, expected post-arrival regional distribution:
1) Conservative (minimize cash burn, higher reliance on fallback lanes)
- Strategy: buy only to maintain a 6–8 week effective safety buffer at 65% utilization; rely on cloud-burst + short leases for peak.
- Action: place small A100 and L40 replenishment orders monthly (20–30 units tranche) for Jan–Jun 2026; defer H100 buys until Q2 unless lead time shortens.
- Expected coverage: maintain current net capacity; fill attrition and growth mostly via spot/dedicated cloud contracts.
- Risk: potential SLA degradation in high-growth scenarios; cost exposure to cloud spot premium.

2) Balanced (recommended baseline)
- Strategy: targeted H100 buy to secure model serving headroom + A100/L40 to smooth queue economics. Mix emphasizes 60% high-perf (H100/A100) and 40% cost-efficient.
- Action: commit to two tranches: 
  * Tranche A (PO Jan 2026) — H100 x 160 (split US-W 80 / US-E 40 / EU 25 / APAC 15) — expected arrival Apr–Jun 2026.
  * Tranche B (PO Feb 2026) — A100 x 200 + L40 x 120 (regional split to rebalance utilization) — expected arrival Mar–May 2026.
- Expected outcome: 20–25% increase in serving headroom across regions, headroom for model upgrades and canary rollouts.
- Risk mitigation: include flexible cancellation clauses for A100 tranche; negotiate 2–4 week lead time improvement SLAs with main reseller.

3) Aggressive (capture growth, cost per token reduction)
- Strategy: front-load H100 purchases to lock unit pricing and avoid allocation queues; pair with larger L40 buys to offload batch jobs.
- Action: 1x large PO (Dec 2025 window if pricing lock possible) for H100 x 360 and A100 x 240. Stagger shipments to regions over 6–10 weeks to avoid rack saturation.
- Expected outcome: immediate cost-per-token fall (estimated 15–22% reduction) and capacity to accept large enterprise Dedicated deals.
- Risk: capital lock, potential underutilization if growth slows.

Fallback lanes and short-term capacity (operational playbook):
- Cloud burst partners: pre-negotiated reserved spot capacity with two vendors (Vendor-A for US regions, Vendor-B for APAC/EU) with preemptible pricing cap (we pay up to X% above on-prem).
- Reseller short leases: 3–6 month lease lines from distributor partners used historically to cover 4–8 week procurement gaps.
- Cross-region reallocation: maintain transit buffer of 40–60 GPUs staging in US-W to cover emergency east/eu demand via air-shipment — cost considered last resort.
- Capacity grafting: leverage dedicated GPU “swap boxes” (rented racks) that can be installed in 7–10 days for small bursts.

Reorder points and safety buffer calc (simplified):
- Monthly burn rate estimates (global blended): H100 28 units, A100 45 units, L40 22 units (growth adjusted).
- Safety buffer target: 8–10 weeks of burn for H100, 6–8 weeks for A100, 4–6 weeks for L40.
- Example reorder point (US-W H100): current on-hand 220, monthly burn 12 -> reorder when <= 220 - (12 * 8) -> reorder trigger ~124 units. Adjust for transit lead.

Procurement cadence and PO structuring recommendations:
- Use staggered POs to smooth arrivals and avoid datacenter rack overloads (max 120 GPUs per week install target).
- Negotiate partial-ship and rolling-invoice terms to align cash flow with delivery.
- Include specified lead time SLAs and liquidated damages for >20% slippage beyond stated bands.
- Insist on serial-number-level delivery visibility and manifest 2 weeks prior to ship.

Cost and headcount implications:
- Hardware capital cap: $12M default (Jan–Jun 2026). Estimated cost bands per unit (street rates Oct 2025): H100 ~$22k, A100 ~$12k, L40 ~$8k, RTX ~$3.5k. Numbers vary by bulk discounts and trade-in credits.
- Install / staging headcount: plan for 3–4 week install sprints; each 120-GPU install requires 2 infra techs full-time + 1 SRE liaison for deployment pipelines.

Immediate open questions / blockers (action items):
- A: Procurement to confirm allocation windows with primary H100 reseller by 2025-11-20 (owner: Jason Nguyen, JIRA ENGINFRA-512).
- B: Finance to confirm capital availability and willing-to-size for aggressive tranche by 2025-11-30.
- C: SRE to validate maximum weekly install cap and expedite checklist (owner: Marco Silva).
- D: Legal to review addendum for partial shipment SLA and penalty clauses.

Notes to self / rough ideas: 
- Consider a small pilot of vendor-direct consignment in EU to reduce lead time for critical bursts.
- Explore model-to-hardware matching table (model families -> preferred SKU + quantization profile) to avoid overbuying H100 for batch-only workloads.
- Keep record of historical lead time slips in spreadsheet (attach to Confluence page) to refine reorder point calc next quarter.

References / links:
- Confluence: Fleet-Procurement-Playbook-2025 (linked)
- JIRA: ENGINFRA-512 (H100 allocation) | ENGINFRA-487 (Install ops backlog)
- PR: infra/pulls/289 (install automation for rack mapping)

Versioning and next steps:
- This is draft v0.9 — incorporate procurement feedback and vendor lead-time confirms. Next review: 2025-12-08 working session (invite infra + procurement + finance).

Appendix: quick reorder example (numeric)
- US-W H100 current 220, monthly burn 12, lead time expected 20 weeks -> to cover 20 weeks + 8 weeks safety need 28 * 12 = 336?? (note: calculation shorthand; please verify).

(Deliberately rough math above — use linked spreadsheet for precise reorder point / cashflow modeling.)

-- end of working sheet (notes, placeholders and TODOs intentionally left).
